CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal renal ultrasound with atrophic right kidney.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
14-year-old female previously healthy who presented with acute onset right-sided abdominal pain and nausea/vomiting. Initial evaluation at local urgent care for presumed gastroenteritis. Symptoms worsened the following day. Repeat evaluation with ultrasound revealed one kidney significantly smaller than the other. Patient was referred to Jacksonville where imaging confirmed atrophic right kidney with cysts noted on kidney and ovaries. Swollen lymph nodes and infection were also identified. Patient was subsequently seen in Atlanta where she received treatment. Since that time, vomiting has resolved but patient continues to report abdominal pain and burning sensation, particularly when eating. Mother reports patient had recurrent hospitalizations at age 4 with fevers and similar symptoms occurring several times over a couple-month period, then resolved. Mother suspects possible prior kidney infection affecting right kidney development. Patient currently reports mild abdominal pain and burning on urination, particularly with certain beverages like soda. Denies hematuria.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Mild abdominal pain and burning sensation, especially when eating. Dysuria with certain beverages, particularly carbonated drinks. Denies hematuria. No current vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Recurrent fevers and hospitalizations at age 4 (approximately 3-4 times, 3 days per episode over a couple-month period). Atrophic right kidney. Cysts on kidney and ovaries. Prior evaluation by GI and geneticist with no clinically significant mutations identified on genetic panel.

MEDICATIONS
Pepcid 40 mg daily
Claritin as needed for allergies

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father: Deceased at age 47 from massive heart attack. Had posterior urethral valves with obstructive neuropathy (congenital), developed chronic kidney disease, was dialysis-dependent, and received a renal transplant which subsequently failed.
Maternal grandfather: Posterior urethral valves with obstructive neuropathy, chronic kidney disease, dialysis-dependent, renal transplant with subsequent failure.
Maternal great aunt: End-stage renal disease, chronic kidney disease stage 5, diabetes, hypertension (diagnosed in adulthood).
Maternal cousins: Kidney disease.
Maternal grandmother: Breast cancer.
Renal disease runs in maternal family.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Active in softball. Interested in joining drill team over summer. Lives with parents.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing 14-year-old female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably, not in acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Not examined in detail.
Remainder of exam: Within normal limits.

RESULTS
Renal ultrasound: Right kidney atrophic (smaller than left kidney). Left kidney appears enlarged, possibly compensatory. Cysts noted on right kidney and ovaries. Lymph nodes enlarged.
Renal function: Normal.
Blood pressure: Normal.
Urinalysis: Pending monitoring for proteinuria and hematuria.
Genetic testing: No clinically significant mutations identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
14-year-old with history of atrophic right kidney, likely secondary to prior severe infection in early childhood. Currently asymptomatic from a renal function standpoint with normal kidney function and blood pressure.

Plan:
1. Annual monitoring with renal ultrasound to assess kidney size and function.
2. Annual urinalysis to screen for proteinuria and hematuria.
3. Annual blood pressure check.
4. Avoid nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); use acetaminophen instead.
5. Maintain adequate hydration with at least 2 liters of water daily, especially during sports activities.
6. Continue healthy diet and active lifestyle.
7. Continue current medications (Pepcid and Claritin).
8. Follow-up with primary care physician or adult nephrologist at home on annual basis.
9. Parents instructed to call if symptoms worsen.
